compression.title: Database Compression
compression.desc: Migrate historical request bodies from plaintext into a deduplicated compressed form. Each run rewrites one batch and can be paused; an interrupted run resumes from its watermark.
compression.original_hint: Total original bytes across the table, measured once when a run starts
compression.original_unmeasured: Not measured yet: one "Start migration" measures it (reads record headers only, changes nothing)
compression.stored_hint: Size the database file actually occupies on disk (including not-yet-reclaimed free space — see "Reclaimable")
compression.ratio_running: Migration in progress: this climbs as rows change form (starts near 1.0×)
compression.reclaimable_hint_off: Freed but still inside the file. With auto_vacuum=0 the file only grows; VACUUM is required to return this to disk.
compression.reclaimable_hint_on: Freed and returnable to disk via incremental vacuum.
compression.rows_hint: Told apart by whether the column holds plaintext or a frame
compression.blocks_hint: Groups total {{size}} on disk; each block row is shared by several bodies
compression.db_unavailable: Database stats unavailable (the migration is writing and this read hit the lock) — it retries automatically, no refresh needed
compression.db_unavailable_short: Database stats are temporarily unavailable; they refresh automatically
compression.db_stale: Database stats measured at {{time}} (too busy to measure right now)

reclaim.label: Reclaim:
reclaim.how: Triggered by: {{source}} · Stopped because: {{reason}} · Took {{duration}} · Ran {{calls}} statements
reclaim.cost: Reclaim blocks writes to the database for its whole duration: write requests queue, and any that cannot get write access within 5 seconds fail. Reads are unaffected. Each round runs for at most 90 seconds; the remainder is left for next time.
reclaim.title: Reclaim free pages in the database
reclaim.desc: Return the free pages already released inside the database file to the filesystem. This does not modify data; it can be run repeatedly and can be interrupted.
reclaim.step_1: 512 reclaim statements per batch, one transaction per batch
reclaim.step_2: Each round runs for at most 90 seconds and leaves the remainder for next time, so several rounds may be needed and one click may not finish it
reclaim.eta: Estimated from the {{size}} reclaimable right now: about {{rounds}} rounds, roughly {{eta}} in total. The database frees one page at a time; measured at about 1,500 pages/s on average, slower in the early rounds.
reclaim.warn: During this time, write requests (including logs) queue, and any that cannot get write access within 5 seconds fail. Reads are unaffected.
reclaim.why: Why this is slower than VACUUM: it processes one page at a time, and freeing a page requires moving the file's last page into that position. For 5 GiB of free space, reclaiming it gradually takes about 15 minutes (with the service running), whereas VACUUM takes 56 seconds (but requires downtime and free disk space twice the size of the database file). To clear it in one go, start once with DB_VACUUM=true.
reclaim.continuous_hint: When off, only one round runs (90 seconds at most).
reclaim.continuous_help: For 5 GiB of free space, having this off means running it a dozen times or more to clear it. When on, the service pauses for 0.1 seconds between batches, so write requests queue and then succeed; when off, there is no pause and write requests during those 90 seconds fail outright.
reclaim.step_continuous: 512 reclaim statements per batch, one transaction per batch; a 0.1-second pause between batches, running until finished (or until you press Stop)
reclaim.eta_continuous: Estimated from the {{size}} reclaimable right now: about {{rounds}} batches, roughly {{eta}} in total, including the pauses between batches. Later batches are faster; this is an average.
reclaim.warn_continuous: Writes to the database are blocked while it runs, but there is a 0.1-second pause between batches: write requests queue and slow down rather than fail — the longest wait is about one batch (measured 0.3–4.4 seconds, under the 5-second timeout). Reads are unaffected.
reclaim.auto_on: Auto reclaim: when reclaimable space exceeds {{size}}, checked every {{min}} minutes
reclaim.policy_desc: Whether the service reclaims space automatically in the background. Off by default — reclaim blocks writes to the database while it runs, which users can notice, so when the database may be occupied is your decision.
reclaim.policy_switch_hint: When on, reclaim runs automatically on the threshold and interval set below.
reclaim.policy_switch_help: Automatic runs always use "Reclaim continuously until finished", so writes briefly slow down while it runs, but they do not fail.
reclaim.min_bytes_hint: Reclaim does not run below this value.
reclaim.min_bytes_help: In bytes. The default is 268435456 (256 MiB) and the maximum is 1 TiB. When the free space in the database is below this value, automatic reclaim does not start, so that a very small amount of space does not claim write access.
reclaim.check_interval_hint: How often reclaimable space is checked.
reclaim.check_interval_help: In seconds; 60–86400 is accepted and the default is 3600 (1 hour). Values outside the range are adjusted to the nearest allowed value. Each check reads the free page count once and does not affect normal writes.
reclaim.policy_continuous_note: Automatic reclaim always runs as "Reclaim continuously until finished": at one 90-second round per cycle, 5 GiB of free space would take ten cycles to clear, which makes automating it pointless. While an automatic run is in progress, writes briefly slow down, but they do not fail.

reason.empty: All free space has been reclaimed
reason.budget: This round's time is up; the remainder is left for next time
reason.no_auto_vacuum: This database does not have auto_vacuum enabled, so reclaim has no effect
reason.stalled: This batch freed no free pages, so it ended early (see the error below for details)
reason.stopped: Stopped manually (takes effect between batches; the current batch still finishes)
reason.busy: The migration task has higher priority, so reclaim gave up the database maintenance lock
reason.vacuumed: VACUUM was run at service start
reason.insufficient_space: Not enough disk space, skipped (the service started normally)

blocked.busy_migration: A migration task is running and reclaim must wait — they share the same maintenance lock.
blocked.no_stats: The database status cannot be read right now, so it cannot be confirmed whether any free space exists.
blocked.no_auto_vacuum: This database has auto_vacuum=0, so reclaim has no effect (measured: 0 seconds, file size unchanged). To shrink the file, run VACUUM once on the whole database; or start once with DB_AUTO_VACUUM_REBUILD=on to convert it to INCREMENTAL.
blocked.nothing: There is no space to reclaim — the database contains no free pages.

backup.label: Backup detection:
backup.stale: The backup detected is smaller than the current database and may be a stale pre-migration backup — restoring it would lose data
backup.forced: Run without a backup after operator confirmation

compression.policy_disabled: Automatic progress: off (manual runs still work)
compression.no_backup_desc: Migration rewrites the storage form of historical request bodies in place. The simplest way to recover if something goes wrong is to restore from a backup, which requires that a backup exists.
compression.no_backup_hint: The safer approach is to copy the database file first, then return here and click "Start migration". If you continue, this run is recorded as having had no backup.
compression.run_desc: Rewrite historical request bodies from plaintext into the compressed form (4 KiB chunks, globally deduplicated; each row keeps only a list of chunk ids). Rows are rewritten in place, not copied.
compression.run_step_1: 64 rows / 32 MiB per batch, one transaction per batch; you can press Pause at any time and it stops once the current batch finishes
compression.run_step_2: After an interruption (closing the page, exiting the program, power loss), the next start continues from where it left off — work already done is not repeated
compression.run_step_3: The service keeps running throughout: reads are unaffected; a write request waits at most about 0.2 seconds per batch
compression.run_step_4: Logs written from now on are stored in compressed form immediately; they do not wait for this run to finish
compression.run_eta: Estimated time {{eta}}: {{rows}} rows left to migrate, at the measured rate of about {{rate}} rows/s (actual speed depends on the disk)
compression.run_cost_1: Reads return data identical byte for byte — losslessness was verified by a full-database round trip (12,483 rows / 6.06 GiB compared in full, 0 mismatches)
compression.run_cost_2: The only way back is "Revert to plaintext": it resets migration progress and makes the database file substantially larger
compression.rollback_desc: Restore every compressed request body to plaintext. This is a complete rewrite of the database.
compression.rollback_step_1: Scans the whole table and writes each row's compressed data back as plaintext in place; one transaction per batch
compression.rollback_step_2: Reads are unaffected; write requests queue and slow down
compression.rollback_eta: Estimated time {{eta}}: {{rows}} rows are still in compressed form, at the measured rate of about {{rate}} rows/s
compression.rollback_warn: The database file grows substantially (measured: 1.46 GiB → 7.12 GiB), and space reclaim cannot win it back — a VACUUM is required to return it to disk.
compression.rollback_reset: When the revert finishes, migration progress is reset to "never run": you must click "Start migration" again and run it through completely to return to the compressed form.
compression.edit_desc: These settings control how much data is processed per batch; they do not affect compression. Chunk and group sizes are fixed in code, and changing them would make already-stored data unreadable.
compression.policy_switch_hint: When on, the service periodically continues an unfinished migration. Manually clicking "Start migration" is unaffected by this switch.
compression.policy_switch_help: When on, the service continues an unfinished migration automatically at the interval set below. Turn it off if the migration should only run when you start it yourself.
compression.batch_rows_hint: How many rows are processed per batch.
compression.batch_rows_help: 1–4096 is accepted; values outside the range are adjusted to the nearest allowed value. A larger value compresses each group better, but also reads more raw data into memory at once.
compression.batch_bytes_hint: The size limit processed per batch.
compression.batch_bytes_help: The current batch ends when this limit is reached. Whatever the setting, each batch processes at least one row.
compression.batch_interval_hint: How long to pause between batches.
compression.batch_interval_help: 0–5000 milliseconds is accepted; values outside the range are adjusted to the nearest allowed value. This controls the share of time the migration occupies the database, not its speed: a larger value leaves the database idle more and makes the migration take longer.
compression.quiesce_hint: Rows written recently are not processed.
compression.quiesce_help: In seconds. Rows written within this period are excluded from the migration, so that records that have not finished being written are never processed.

toast.started: Migration started and is running in the background
toast.paused: Pause requested; it stops once the current batch finishes
toast.rollback_started: Revert started and is running in the background
